title: Two ample principal affine opens avoiding an orbit boundary
statement: Let $Y$ be a nonempty Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], with topological Krull dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $L$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], and let $G$ be a finite group acting on $Y$ by scheme automorphisms. No base field, separatedness or faithfulness is assumed. For a section $s$ of an invertible module put $Y_s=\{y:s(y)\ne0\}$, where $s(y)$ is its value in the residue-field fibre [def-weil-residue-field], and let $Z(s)=Y\setminus Y_s$. The set $E$ of generic points of irreducible components of $Y$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] is finite and nonempty. There exist positive integers $p,q$ and sections $u\in\Gamma(Y,L^{\otimes p})$, $v\in\Gamma(Y,L^{\otimes q})$ such that $U=Y_u$ and $V=Y_v$ are affine, $E\subseteq U\cap V$, $Z=Y\setminus U$ is a finite set of closed points of $Y$, and the finite set $T=\bigcup_{g\in G}g^{-1}Z$ satisfies $h^{-1}T=T$ for every $h\in G$ and $T\subseteq V$.

source.place: Agent construction from Tag 09NV (lemma-ample-finite-set-in-principal-affine), applied first to the component generic points and then to their union with the orbit boundary. This is the preparation in original steps 1-4 of the item, serving de Jong §3.4(b); the complete retained argument and other local sources are in the repair report.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], the underlying space of $Y$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] to the closed subset $Y$: its irreducible components form a finite covering $C_1,\ldots,C_r$. Since $Y$ is nonempty, $r>0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober], each $C_i$ has exactly one generic point $\eta_i$. Thus $E=\{\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r\}$ is finite and nonempty. Sobriety also implies $T_0$: equal point closures would have two generic points unless the points were equal.

source.place: Tag 09NV, lemma-ample-finite-set-in-principal-affine, applied twice; Noetherian component and dimension argument using Tags 01OZ, 0BA8, 0AAX and Schemes Tag 01IS

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-ample-finite-principal-affine] to the ample module $L$, the finite subset $E$, and the open $W=Y$. Obtain $p>0$ and $u\in\Gamma(Y,L^{\otimes p})$ with $U=Y_u$ affine and $E\subseteq U$. In particular $Z=Y\setminus U$ is closed and contains no $\eta_i$.

source.place: Tag 09NV, lemma-ample-finite-set-in-principal-affine, applied twice; Noetherian component and dimension argument using Tags 01OZ, 0BA8, 0AAX and Schemes Tag 01IS

proof.text: We check $\dim Z\le0$ directly from [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. If $A\subsetneq B$ were irreducible closed subsets of $Z$, they would be irreducible closed in $Y$ since $Z$ is closed. As $B=\bigcup_i(B\cap C_i)$ is a finite closed cover, irreducibility forces $B\subseteq C_i$ for some $i$. Moreover $B\ne C_i$, since $\eta_i\notin Z$. Then $A\subsetneq B\subsetneq C_i$ is a length-two chain in $Y$, contradicting $\dim Y\le1$. Thus no positive-length chain exists in $Z$ (including $Z=\varnothing$). Now apply [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-closed-finite] to this closed subset of the Noetherian $T_0$ space established in step 1: $Z$ is finite and every point of $Z$ is closed in $Y$.

source.place: Tag 09NV, lemma-ample-finite-set-in-principal-affine, applied twice; Noetherian component and dimension argument using Tags 01OZ, 0BA8, 0AAX and Schemes Tag 01IS

proof.text: For each $g\in G$, the action of $g$ is a bijection with inverse the action of $g^{-1}$, so $g^{-1}Z$ is the image of the finite set $Z$ under this inverse bijection. Therefore $T=\bigcup_{g\in G}g^{-1}Z$ is finite. For every $h\in G$, $h^{-1}T=\bigcup_{g\in G}(gh)^{-1}Z=T$, since right multiplication $g\mapsto gh$ permutes $G$. This uses only finite unions and the action law; no faithfulness is needed.

source.place: Tag 09NV, lemma-ample-finite-set-in-principal-affine, applied twice; Noetherian component and dimension argument using Tags 01OZ, 0BA8, 0AAX and Schemes Tag 01IS

proof.text: The set $E\cup T$ is finite. Apply [lem-sc-ample-finite-principal-affine] again, with the same ample module $L$ and open $W=Y$, to obtain $q>0$ and $v\in\Gamma(Y,L^{\otimes q})$ with $V=Y_v$ affine and $E\cup T\subseteq V$. Consequently $E\subseteq U\cap V$ and $T\subseteq V$, which supplies all remaining clauses.

Shape: one commit; the statement is the same as on the base and only split-owned fields change; no new nodes; no SGA cited. Source: I read Stacks Tag 09NV (properties.tex line 5293). It matches lem-sc-ample-finite-principal-affine hypothesis by hypothesis: any scheme, ample L, a finite set inside an open W, giving n>0 and s with X_s affine. Tag 0AAX was read for the zero-dimensional node. The parent pencil node's step 1 uses exactly the item's p, q, u, v, U, V and T. Step 1: the minimal-element property gives a Noetherian space. The finite-components node writes Y as a finite union of components, and every component is one of them by maximality (two lines, left implicit). Sobriety gives unique generic points, so E is finite and nonempty, and it also gives T0 (equal closures would have two generic points). Step 2: 09NV is applied to E with W=Y. Step 3: an irreducible B in Z lies in some C_i, and B is not C_i because η_i is not in Z. So A⊊B⊊C_i would be a chain of length 2, which contradicts dim Y≤1. The zero-dimensional lemma then makes Z finite with points closed in Y; Z empty is allowed. Step 4 (elementary): h^{-1}g^{-1}Z=(gh)^{-1}Z, so T is invariant under every h without faithfulness, and the same works for a right action. Step 5: 09NV is applied to E∪T. Edge cases checked: Spec k; P^1 over F_2 with PGL_2(F_2), where q≠p is needed; an isolated point; and P^2, which shows dim≤1 is necessary. No duplicate found by rg -L search for 09NV, ample-finite and orbit+affine. The tool_uses for 09NV and for the zero-dimensional closed-finite node are accepted as generic curve-estimates tools.
